'''''Heliotropium europaeum''''' is a species of [[Heliotropium|heliotrope]] known by the common names '''European heliotrope'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=HEEU|taxon=Heliotropium europaeum|accessdate=19 January 2016}}</ref> and '''European turn-sole'''.<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref>

== Description ==
''Heliotropium europaeum'' is an [[annual herb]] growing from a [[taproot]] and reaching maximum heights near {{Convert|40|cm|sp=us}}. The stem and oval-shaped leaves are covered in soft hairs. The [[inflorescence]]s are coiled spikes of fragrant, white flowers with fuzzy or bristly [[sepal]]s. Each flower is just a few millimeters wide. The fruit is a bumpy nutlet.

== Distribution and habitat ==
The species is native to Eurasia and North Africa, but it is widely [[introduced species|naturalized]] elsewhere, such as in Australia and North America. It grows as a roadside weed in some places.

==Toxicity==
It contains [[pyrrolizidine alkaloid]]s and is [[poisonous]].<ref name=MERCK>[http://www.merckvetmanual.com/mvm/htm/bc/ttox05.htm  The MERCK Veterinary Manual, Table 5] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101117170853/http://www.merckvetmanual.com/mvm/htm/bc/ttox05.htm |date=2010-11-17 }}</ref>
